q: The Constitution of India came into effect on which date?
exp: The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day). Answer: 26 January 1950

q: Who is known as the Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is called the Chief Architect of the Constitution. Answer: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

q: How many Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
exp: There are 6 Fundamental Rights (after the right to property ceased to be fundamental in 1978). Answer: 6

q: The Preamble declares India to be a what?
exp: The Preamble (as amended in 1976) declares India a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic. Answer: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic

q: Which article of the Constitution deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
exp: Article 32 (called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Ambedkar) guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies. Answer: Article 32

q: The idea of the Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from the constitution of?
exp: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution. Answer: Ireland

q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
exp: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner. Answer: President

q: The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum strength of how many members?
exp: The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) can have a maximum of 250 members (238 elected + 12 nominated). Answer: 250

q: Which schedule of the Constitution contains the anti-defection law?
exp: The Tenth Schedule (added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985) contains the anti-defection law. Answer: Tenth Schedule

q: The National Emergency can be declared under which article?
exp: Article 352 deals with a National Emergency on grounds of war/aggression/internal disturbance. Answer: Article 352

q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists how many languages?
exp: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages; it now lists 22 languages. Answer: 22

q: Which amendment is called the 'Mini-Constitution' of India?
exp: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the Mini-Constitution for its sweeping changes. Answer: 42nd Amendment

q: The concept of Judicial Review in India is borrowed from which country?
exp: Judicial Review was borrowed from the USA (Marbury v. Madison tradition). Answer: USA

q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India on which date?
exp: GST was rolled out nationwide on 1 July 2017 via the 101st Amendment. Answer: 1 July 2017

q: The Panchayati Raj system was constitutionalised by which amendment?
exp: The 73rd Amendment (1992) constitutionalised the Panchayati Raj system. Answer: 73rd Amendment
